candidates.attacker_control: The entry names come from dependency jars on the build classpath: any third-party jar (regular dependency or WebJar, e.g. a compromised/malicious artifact published to Maven Central or bundled by a compromised component) can contain entries with `../` after the expected base path. The build only validates the prefix, not the resolved path.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked whether the prefix filter prevents traversal: it does not, because `../` may appear after the required base path. Checked whether any later normalization/containment validation exists in JarContentsManager or ProductionModeCopyStep: none (no Path.normalize/getCanonicalFile/startsWith check on the resolved destination). Checked whether the excluded-file wildcard filter helps: it only filters entry names, not the resulting relative path. The code path is not guarded by any authentication/role check (it is a build step). Note the source appears consistent with long-standing upstream code, so this may be an unfixed historical defect rather than a reverted security patch.
candidates.impact: Arbitrary file write (subject to the build process's permissions) outside the intended frontend/output directory on the machine running the production build — e.g. overwriting project files, build configuration, scripts or user files, which can be escalated to code execution in the build/CI environment. No source-text path normalization or containment check exists to prevent it.
candidates.prerequisites: A build using the affected flow-maven-plugin production-mode goal with a dependency jar containing crafted entry names; the plugin must run (developer/CI machine) for the write to occur. WebJar handling additionally requires the jar to contain a bower.json/package.json under META-INF/resources/webjars/ so it is treated as a WebJar.
candidates.root_cause: JarContentsManager.copyJarEntryTrimmingBasePath() derives the destination path directly from the jar entry name. It only checks that the entry name startsWith the configured base path (in the caller), then computes `relativePath = fullPath.substring(indexOf(basePath) + basePath.length())` and writes to `new File(outputDirectory, relativePath)` (line 183) with no normalization and no check that the result stays inside `outputDirectory`. A jar entry such as `META-INF/resources/frontend/../../../../../../tmp/x` passes the `startsWith(basePath)` filter, yields `../../../../../../tmp/x`, and escapes the output directory when `FileUtils.copyInputStreamToFile` creates parent folders and writes. ProductionModeCopyStep.copyWebApplicationFiles() invokes this for every regular dependency jar (base `META-INF/resources/frontend`, lines 198-200) and for each WebJar package directory (line 194).
candidates.title: Zip Slip: jar entries are extracted without path normalization, allowing arbitrary file write outside the target directory during production builds
candidates.trace: ProductionModeCopyStep.copyWebApplicationFiles(outputDirectory, ...) -> JarContentsManager.copyFilesFromJarTrimmingBasePath(jar, basePath, outputDirectory, exclusions) [JarContentsManager.java:146-160] -> stream filters `entryName.toLowerCase().startsWith(basePath.toLowerCase())` -> copyJarEntryTrimmingBasePath(jarFile, jarEntry, basePath, outputDirectory) [178-187] -> `relativePath = fullPath.substring(... + basePath.length())` (line 180-181, no `..`/absolute-path handling) -> FileUtils.copyInputStreamToFile(input, new File(outputDirectory, relativePath)) (line 183) -> write outside outputDirectory for crafted entry names. The same class's getPackageName()/caller line 192 also use the WebJar-declared package name (substring after the last '/') as a file name, so a bower.json name ending in `/..` also yields `..` as a directory component.
candidates.unverified: Not built or executed (no build/run tools permitted); the write primitive and escape were established by reading the source, not by running a crafted jar. I could not verify against the fixed upstream version (no network/git history in this run), so it is unconfirmed whether this exact code was later patched or is the snapshot's intended finding.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-22 Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal') / Zip Slip (arbitrary file write)

coverage_summary: Snapshot: Vaadin Flow 1.3-SNAPSHOT, 1,352 files (1,073 Java); module POMs reviewed for module layout. Read/traced in detail: flow-server request pipeline (VaadinServlet, VaadinServletService, VaadinService, VaadinSession, StaticFileServer, WebJarServer, BootstrapHandler/BootstrapUtils/InitialPageSettings/InlineTargets, ServerRpcHandler + all rpc/* handlers, UidlRequestHandler/UidlWriter, StreamRequestHandler/StreamReceiverHandler/StreamResourceHandler, PushHandler/PushRequestHandler/JSR356WebsocketInitializer, PwaHandler/PwaRegistry/PwaIcon/PwaConfiguration, HeartbeatHandler, UnsupportedBrowserHandler, ServletHelper, ServletDeployer-related startup classes, router Location/ParameterDeserializer/DefaultRouteResolver), flow-client binding/communication/error code, flow-data DataCommunicator area, flow-theme-integrations, and the flow-maven-plugin (JarContentsManager, ProductionModeCopyStep, FrontendDataProvider, FrontendToolsLocator/Manager, BundleConfigurationReader, ComponentGeneratorPlugin). Relation index coverage is partial (1,050-1,051 parsed files of 1,350, 2 omitted, no semantic resolution/data flow/control flow; 16,689 unresolved call candidates), so index-derived navigation was always verified against source text. Large periphery (generated components, resources/JS bundles, OSGi/tests modules) was sampled rather than read exhaustively.
limitations: No build, test execution, scanners, or runtime verification was allowed; the finding is based on static reading only and is a lead, not a confirmed vulnerability.
No unit/integration test sources are present in the snapshot (flow-server/src/test and generator tests absent), so intended behavior could not be confirmed from tests.

No git history, upstream comparison, CVE/advisory lookup, or web access was available, so I could not determine whether the candidate was later patched or whether it is the snapshot's intended vulnerability.
The P1 relation index is syntactic and partial (no data flow, control flow, or semantic resolution); its security_call/config facts are navigation hints only and were not treated as findings.
Some areas were sampled rather than fully reviewed (generated component classes, client resources / minified JS, OSGi and test-fixture modules); a vulnerability could exist there undetected.

rejected_leads.lead: ElementPropertyMap.deferredUpdateFromClient (flow-server/src/main/java/com/vaadin/flow/internal/nodefeature/ElementPropertyMap.java:78-100) rejects a property update only when `updateFromClientFilter != null && !updateFromClientFilter.test(key)`; otherwise it falls through to `putWithDeferredChangeEvent`, so a forged `mapSync` RPC can write properties that are neither synchronized nor allowed (including the `forbiddenProperties` textContent/classList/className) into the server-side property map of the attacker's own UI.
rejected_leads.reason: Strong code smell (the code's own warning states the 'for security reasons' policy) but plausibly intentional upstream design for client-side element property defaults, and impact is confined to the attacker's own UI state; I could not confirm it deviates from the fixed upstream code. Reported as an unconfirmed lead, not the candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: UidlWriter.getInlineResourceStream (flow-server/src/main/java/com/vaadin/flow/server/communication/UidlWriter.java:262-295) falls back to `new URL(url).openConnection().getInputStream()` for INLINE dependencies whose URL cannot be resolved from the servlet context (potential SSRF / local file read via file: URLs).
rejected_leads.reason: The URL originates from server-side dependency declarations (@HtmlImport/@JavaScript/@StyleSheet, theme/URL translation), not from a web request, so an unauthenticated remote attacker does not control it; rejected as a remote vulnerability.

rejected_leads.lead: WebJarServer.getWebJarPath (flow-server/src/main/java/com/vaadin/flow/server/webjar/WebJarServer.java:141-146) uses `path.replace(prefix, "/webjars/")` on the request path and passes the result to ServletContext.getResource, and StaticFileServer passes raw request path info to getStaticResource.
rejected_leads.reason: Path resolution/normalization is delegated to the servlet container and the request must start with the configured frontend prefix; I found no source-level evidence that `..` survives container normalization, so no concrete traversal is demonstrated. Unconfirmed lead.

rejected_leads.lead: FrontendDataProvider.createFragmentFile (flow-maven-plugin/src/main/java/com/vaadin/flow/plugin/common/FrontendDataProvider.java:285-300) resolves the fragment file name (`fragmentName + ".html"`) directly against the target directory, allowing `../` escapes if a fragment name in the bundle-configuration file or Maven configuration contains traversal sequences.
rejected_leads.reason: Same class of issue as the candidate but the name comes from the project's own build configuration (self-inflicted), so it is a weaker variant of the same root cause and was not submitted separately.

rejected_leads.lead: ServerRpcHandler.getMessage (flow-server/src/main/java/com/vaadin/flow/server/communication/ServerRpcHandler.java:388-402) reads the entire RPC body into memory without an application-level size limit (64 KiB is only the read buffer and the hash truncation length).
rejected_leads.reason: Typical servlet containers cap POST size by default and the impact is availability-only; no source evidence of a missing framework-level limit relative to intended behavior. Unconfirmed lead.

rejected_leads.lead: Client-side DOM sinks such as SystemErrorHandler.setInnerHTML (flow-client/src/main/java/com/vaadin/client/SystemErrorHandler.java:144-174) render server-provided error text as HTML in non-production mode.
rejected_leads.reason: The content is generated for the same client that triggered the error (self-XSS in debug mode); no cross-user attacker-controlled path could be demonstrated from source. Unconfirmed lead.

summary: Reviewed the Vaadin Flow 1.3-SNAPSHOT source tree (1,352 files; 1,073 Java). I traced the main untrusted-input paths: servlet/UIDL/RPC handling (ServerRpcHandler, UidlRequestHandler, UidlWriter, MapSyncRpcHandler, PublishedServerEventHandlerRpcHandler), bootstrap-page generation (BootstrapHandler/BootstrapUtils/InitialPageSettings), stream resource and file-upload handling (StreamRequestHandler/StreamReceiverHandler/StreamResourceHandler), push (PushHandler/PushRequestHandler), servlet static/webjar serving, PWA handling, routing/Location, and the client-side Flow bindings. The core request-handling paths are generally hardened (CSRF check on RPC, random UUID security keys, Location `..` rejection, `<` escaping of the initial UIDL, PWA workbox path slash-stripping, quote stripping in PWA cache entries). The single strongest concrete defect I found is an unvalidated path in the production-build copy step: jar-entry names are used to build destination files without any normalization, so entries containing `../` write outside the intended output directory (classic Zip Slip, CWE-22). I report that as one candidate and list other plausible-but-unconfirmed leads separately.
